questions.prompt:
A student council polled lunch votes: Pasta 54, Taco 71, Sandwich 38, Salad 47.
Which choice was **most frequent**?

Weekly bike trips recorded Monday through Friday: 5, 7, 2, 4, 12 trips.
Calculate the **mean** (average) trips across those five days.

The same five readings: 5, 7, 2, 4, 12.
Sorted order: 2, 4, 5, 7, 12.
The **median** is which value?

A line graph tracks midday °C Monday–Friday:
Mon 18°, Tue 20°, Wed 26°, Thu 29°, Fri 28°.
Which **one-day change** warmed the fastest?

A pictograph’s key: one oak leaf drawing = eight seedlings pledged.
The Oak Grove row draws **exactly two full oak leaves plus one clearly half-sized leaf.**
How many seedlings?

Two posters both cite cafeteria ratings near **93% happy**.
Poster A graphs bars stretching from a **90% baseline** topping at **93%.**
Poster B graphs from **0%** up to **93%.**
Reading the labelled percentages honestly, why might Poster **A mislead careless viewers**?
choices: Because truncating vertical axes can inflate how dramatic small wins look visually
Because Poster B forbids quoting numbers
Because bar charts cannot show percentages ever
Because Poster A secretly measures happiness in metres
questions.answer: Because truncating vertical axes can inflate how dramatic small wins look visually

questions.prompt:
You want to compare **April rainfall THIS year versus LAST year** across **five named cities**, each plotted along the horizontal axis.
Which plan matches common classroom practice?
choices: Separate bars (or clustered bars) pairing the two April totals beside each city
Pie charts with wedges labelled “happiness percentage” unrelated to rain
Line graph connecting alphabetical city names pretending they behave like clocks
Dot plot numbering countries from 1–5 only
questions.answer: Separate bars (or clustered bars) pairing the two April totals beside each city

questions.prompt:
Halftime tally (210 fans total): Cheer 126, Chill 54, Wander 30 near concessions.
**Simplified fraction** cheering among **all** polled fans?

Score bins from a graded lab (students per interval):

• 71–75 marks → 28 students
• 76–80 marks → 31 students
• 81–85 marks → 36 students
• 86–90 marks → 24 students

Which interval holds the **mode class** (“most crowded bin”)?

School clubs Monday signup tallies:

• Robotics: 48
• Ecology: 61
• Drama: 53
• Chess: 43

How many **more Ecology than Robotics** students signed?

Seven friends quiz scores (percents):
88, 92, 92, 93, 93, 93, 94.
What is the **mode**?

**Figure A — bar chart excerpt:** Classroom Phoenix averages Quiz A = 82, Quiz B = 78. Classroom Nova averages Quiz A = 87, Quiz B = 71.
For **Nova**, how many percentage points separates the two quiz averages?

Regional rainfall (mm):

• March: 54
• April: 42
• May: 42
• June: 58
• July: 46

Which months **tie lowest**?

Fun news headline screams: “Buying ice cream **causes** shark attacks—they rise together each July!” Charts show both spikes each summer beaches.
Most responsible analytic reaction for Grade‑5 sceptics?
choices: Assume ice cream chemically summons sharks
Suspect summertime beach crowds lurk quietly behind BOTH curves
Demand pie charts depicting shark flavours
questions.answer: Suspect summertime beach crowds lurk quietly behind BOTH curves

questions.prompt:
Ms. Rao posts a flashy bar chart—“**Our robotics club doubled in one week!”** Footnote admits chart tracks **Tuesday club block only** ignores virtual members.
What habit makes the infographic more trustworthy?
choices: Clearly state timeframe, sampling limits, plus link raw counts
Remove axis labels entirely to build mystery
Ensure every legend icon equals exactly π students
Replace numbers with unicorn emojis unconditionally
questions.answer: Clearly state timeframe, sampling limits, plus link raw counts
